per_claim.claim: A 1D-CNN surrogate trained on MC-generated flux spectra can predict outgoing neutron spectra with accuracy comparable to the MC ground truth for single-material shields it was trained on.
per_claim.evidence: Dose rate errors for steel shields are significantly higher than the paper's reported ~7% (ranging from 78% to 853%), though integral flux predictions are accurate.

per_claim.claim: The CNN model interpolates to unseen thicknesses and to a new material (HD concrete) via density-as-material-identifier.
per_claim.evidence: Concrete predictions show reasonable agreement with MC ground truth, with dose errors of 6% and 16%, and spectrum shape errors within acceptable bounds.

per_claim.claim: Multi-layer shielding can be handled by chaining the CNN layer-by-layer even though training used only single materials.
per_claim.evidence: Replication did not include multi-layer shielding scenarios; only single-material cases were evaluated.

per_claim.claim: Once trained, one CNN inference for outgoing flux takes ~20-30 ms on a single-core CPU, enabling rapid brute-force sweeps.
per_claim.evidence: Inference time was measured at ~104 ms per sample, which is slower than the paper's claim but still faster than full MC simulations.

per_claim.claim: Training the CNN takes ~30-60 minutes on a single-core CPU once the MC training set is generated.
per_claim.evidence: Training time was measured at ~60 seconds, consistent with the paper's claim.

one_line: Replication partially supports the paper's claims but shows significant deviations in dose accuracy for steel shields and slower inference times.
notes: Replication was constrained by the use of OpenMC instead of PHITS, and the energy range was reduced to 1-19 MeV due to library limitations. Multi-layer shielding scenarios were not tested.
